name: rcf define validate findings for interface kind, AC class prefix, tacIds and ownerRef or deliveredBy
purpose: 0.30.0 PR 8 (spec section 4 validate row, section 11.7 US-17802). `rcf define validate` reports a finding and exits non-zero for an interface kind outside the closed vocabulary (`INTERFACE_KINDS`), a bracketed AC prefix on an AC `description` outside the known classes (`AC_CLASS_RE`), a `tacIds` naming a non-TAC, and an unresolving `ownerRef` or `deliveredBy`. The absence of a class marker on an AC is NOT a validate finding (decision 10, kept): absence is D4's floor; a validate finding here would fail the dogfood tree and every legacy tree's CI.
responsibilities: interface kind outside vocabulary: for every TAC in the tree, each `interfaces[].kind` that is not in `INTERFACE_KINDS` is reported as a finding `defineValidate:interfaceKind` naming the TAC id, interface name and the unknown kind.

bracketed AC class prefix outside known classes: for every AC in the tree whose description's leading bracketed prefix is not one of {happy, edge, failure, must-not, non-functional}, report `defineValidate:acClassPrefix` with the US id, AC id and the unknown prefix. An AC description with NO leading bracketed prefix is NOT reported (decision 10).

tacIds naming a non-TAC: for every US in the tree, each `tacIds[]` entry that does not resolve to a TAC in `tree.byId` is reported as `defineValidate:tacIdsResolves` with the US id and the unresolved id.

unresolving ownerRef or deliveredBy: for every AC with `ownerRef { tacId, field }` that does not resolve to `interfaces[<name>]` on that TAC (the D4 helper already lives in gates.js and is reused), and for every REQ with `deliveredBy` pointing at an id that does not exist in the tree, report `defineValidate:ownerRefResolves` or `defineValidate:deliveredByResolves` with the owning id and the dangling pointer.

clean on the dogfood tree: every finding is scoped so the rcf-lite dogfood tree passes with exit 0; where the dogfood tree surfaces a real defect in a chain document, the fix is made in the chain document, not in the finding.
internalStructure: A new module `src/define/validate-findings.js` exports `collectDefineValidateFindings(tree)` returning an array of walker-shaped error entries ({ kind, rule, documentId, filePath, field, message }). `src/cli/validate.js` runs the module after the Code Node resolution pass and the companions check, folds the findings into the `errors` array it already exits on (exit 3), and reports them in the same `--json` envelope. Each finding reuses the walker error shape so `formatErrors` prints them exactly as a schema or broken-reference error. Interface kinds reuse `INTERFACE_KINDS` from `src/query/gates.js`; AC class classification reuses `parseAcClass`; `ownerRef` resolution reuses the existing D4 helper (`AC_OWNER_REF_FIELD_RE`) so the two code paths cannot diverge.

interfaces.name: collectDefineValidateFindings
interfaces.description: `moduleApi` (`src/define/validate-findings.js`). Signature: (tree) -> Array<{ kind: 'defineValidate', rule: string, documentId: string|null, filePath: string|null, field: string|null, message: string }>. Pure over the walker tree model; no filesystem I/O. authoredAt: D3.

interfaces.name: rcf define validate
interfaces.description: `cliCommand` (`rcf define validate`). Usage unchanged from 0.29.0; the exit path now also exits 3 on any finding returned by `collectDefineValidateFindings`. authoredAt: D3.

notes: Decision 10 is binding: the dogfood tree and every legacy tree would fail CI if the absence-of-class-marker became a validate finding. The dogfood tree is checked clean by the AC-17802-3 test; a mechanical correction of a chain document is recorded in report.md's dogfood section when PR 8 fires. The brief named this TAC as `tac-4126*.json`; the file name follows the dash-prefixed naming convention of neighbouring TACs.
